source_note: Compiled from GMAC's official GMAT Focus Edition exam structure as reported by multiple 2025-2026 coaching/exam-tracker sources (IMS, Career Launcher, Yocket, CrackVerbal, TestNinjas, Manhattan Review), cross-checked Sep 2026. The GMAT Focus Edition (launched Feb 2024) fully replaced the legacy GMAT; the old format with Analytical Writing Assessment (AWA), Integrated Reasoning (IR), Sentence Correction and Geometry is discontinued and no longer accepted by any business school. Always verify against the current mba.com GMAT Focus Edition page before finalising a question bank, since GMAC can revise section timing/weighting between testing cycles.
exam_pattern_note: GMAT Focus Edition: 64 questions total across 3 equally-weighted, section-adaptive sections — Quantitative Reasoning (21 Qs / 45 min), Verbal Reasoning (23 Qs / 45 min), Data Insights (20 Qs / 45 min). Total testing time 2h15m plus one optional 10-min break. Unlike JEE, there are no fixed 'easy/medium/hard' question slots visible to the candidate — difficulty is chosen adaptively by the scoring algorithm question-by-question within each section based on prior responses.

sections.question_format: Problem Solving only (5-option single-correct MCQ). Data Sufficiency, formerly part of Quant, has moved entirely to Data Insights. Geometry has been removed from the syllabus entirely.

subtopics: Number properties: integers, factors, multiples, divisibility, remainders
Averages (arithmetic mean), descriptive statistics (median, mode, range, standard deviation - conceptual)
Simple and compound interest, profit and loss
topics.syllabus_change_note: Data Sufficiency questions built on arithmetic content are no longer scored under Quant; they now appear only in the Data Insights section.

subtopics: Linear equations and systems of linear equations
topics.syllabus_change_note: No calculus or trigonometry; content is capped at roughly a high-school level.

removed_topics: Geometry (lines, angles, triangles, circles, coordinate geometry)

sections.question_format: 5-option single-correct MCQ only. Sentence Correction has been permanently removed.

subtopics: Supporting details and specific fact retrieval
Passages drawn from business, social science, natural science and humanities topics
Complete the argument / fill in the blank reasoning

sections.question_format: Mixed formats: 5-option MCQ (Data Sufficiency), true/false statement grids (Table Analysis), dropdown sentence completion (Graphics Interpretation), linked two-part MCQ (Two-Part Analysis), and MCQ/true-false across multiple source tabs (Multi-Source Reasoning). This section replaced the legacy Integrated Reasoning section and absorbed Data Sufficiency out of the old Quant section.

subtopics: Determine whether Statement 1 alone is sufficient
Determine whether Statement 2 alone is sufficient
Determine whether both statements together are sufficient
Content drawn from the same arithmetic/algebra pool as Quant, but reasoning-only (no need to solve for a final value)
Sortable data tables with multiple columns
True/False or Yes/No judgement on statements about the table
Filtering and sorting to extract relevant rows
Column charts, line graphs, scatterplots, Venn diagrams, bubble charts
Fill-in-the-blank sentence completion via dropdown menus based on the graphic
Trend reading and value estimation from visuals
Two linked/interdependent sub-questions answered from one shared answer table
Can combine quantitative and verbal/logical reasoning in the same prompt
Information spread across 2-3 tabbed sources (text, table, chart)
Mix of standard MCQ and true/false-grid response formats
